statement: The function returns a result r and r is exactly the increasing list of all k-distant indices of nums. Define an index i to be k-distant when 0 <= i < len(nums) and there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[j] = key, and |i - j| <= k. Then: (a) for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), r[t] is k-distant; (b) for every k-distant i there is exactly one t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] = i; (c) for every t with 0 <= t + 1 < len(r), r[t] < r[t + 1]. These conditions characterize r completely.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums). (The original statement says 1 <= k; k = 0 is also allowed here because the supplied examples use it.)

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular it does not fail, panic, index out of bounds, or overflow on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), 0 <= r[t] < len(nums). Thus every value in the returned vector is a valid 0-based index of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every t with 0 <= t + 1 < len(r), r[t] < r[t + 1]. Hence r is strictly increasing.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every t with 0 <= t < len(r) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[j] = key, and |r[t] - j| <= k. Thus every returned index is k-distant.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), if there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[j] = key, and |i - j| <= k, then there exists t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] = i. Thus every k-distant index is returned.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) for which there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[j] = key, and |i - j| <= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) >= 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key, and for every i with max(0, j - k) <= i <= min(len(nums) - 1, j + k), there exists t with 0 <= t < len(r) and r[t] = i. Thus the entire k-neighborhood of every key occurrence is returned.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = key; and 0 <= k <= len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_k_distant_indices(nums1, key, k) returns r1 and find_k_distant_indices(nums2, key, k) returns r2, if for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums1), nums1[j] = key iff nums2[j] = key, then r1 = r2. Thus the answer depends only on the set of positions where the array equals key, not on the other values.
preconditions: For two arrays nums1 and nums2 and the same key and k: len(nums1) = len(nums2) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 1000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums1; and 0 <= k <= len(nums1).

statement: Whenever find_k_distant_indices(nums, key, k1) returns r1 and find_k_distant_indices(nums, key, k2) returns r2, for every t with 0 <= t < len(r1) there exists u with 0 <= u < len(r2) and r2[u] = r1[t]. Thus increasing k can only add indices to the answer.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; key occurs in nums; and 0 <= k1 <= k2 <= len(nums).
